passage:
The worst moment wasn't the meeting. It was that evening, going through our old spreadsheets and realising Tejas had moved the customer list to a new company without telling me. I'm Vinita. Tejas was my closest friend before becoming my co-founder, so I doubted everything: the late nights, the first client, even the jokes.

I was so angry I nearly posted something online. Instead I let myself be sad first. Then I collected facts: dates, emails, the founders' agreement we'd signed. I wrote down what had actually been agreed. The work we built is real, whatever Tejas did. I'm not making any big decisions this week, and when I do, it will be with proper advice and a clear head.

qa.q: What had Tejas moved to a new company?
qa.a: Tejas had moved the customer list to a new company.

qa.q: Why did Vinita doubt everything after the discovery?
qa.a: Tejas was a close friend before becoming co-founder, so the betrayal made Vinita question the late nights, the first client and even the jokes.

qa.q: What steps did Vinita take instead of reacting online?
qa.a: Vinita let sadness come first, collected facts such as dates, emails and the founders' agreement, and put off big decisions until a clear head and proper advice.

qa.q: What would change if Vinita had posted online in anger?
qa.a: It could have turned a private betrayal into a public fight, harming Vinita's own work too and closing off calmer options.

grounding: A co-founder who was a close friend has betrayed Vinita; Vinita separates the sting from the value of the work, gathers facts and avoids panic decisions.
